title: I made an ASCII survivor-like where your tiny triangle grows into a 24-turret Titan. Looking for playtesters (TestFlight)
author: danura_
selftext:
Hey all,

I'm a solo dev and I've been working on Astronormous Survivor, an arcade survivor-like for iPhone. It's now on TestFlight and I'm looking for people to break it.

**The idea**  
You start as a very small ship. Your weapons fire on their own, so you just steer, dodge and dash. Between waves you spend your loot in the hangar, and every weapon you buy gets bolted onto your hull. After 20 minutes your ship looks like a flying junkyard with 24 turrets, and that's the whole fantasy.

• 31 weapons in 6 families (kinetic, energy, explosive, drones, thermal, force fields), with synergies when you stack a family  
• Hull grows through 30 levels, from a nimble core to a Titan  
• Random shop with only 3 offers per visit: reroll, lock and adapt  
• A boss every 5 waves, 10 bosses with their own bullet-hell patterns  
• 10 starting ships, unlocks across runs

**The vibe**  
Strict black & white vector/ASCII look, like a ship's onboard terminal. One rule for readability: anything red wants you dead, anything blue is yours. It gets very busy very fast (see trailer).

**The tech, quickly**  
Built in Godot 4 with the mobile renderer. Made for touch: floating joystick and one-tap dash. Also playable on keyboard. Available in EN/FR/DE/IT/ES.

**What I'd love feedback on**  
• Difficulty curve: where did you die, and did it feel fair?  
• Touch controls: does the joystick or dash ever betray you?  
• Performance on older iPhones when the screen fills with bullets  
• Which builds felt broken (in a good or bad way)

TestFlight link: https://testflight.apple.com/join/3ueN6CaB

Happy to answer anything about the game or the dev side. Thanks for playing!

comments.author: theEsel01
comments.body: Wouldn't it be ascii if all the visuals are made from text?

replies.author: danura_
replies.body: I tried but everything was unreadable, so instead I've used ascii effects and kept a layer with lines on top. Trying to keep the best of two worlds.
